content: The title of the page should be formatted as (Disease name) risk factors, with only the first letter of the title capitalized. The purpose of this page is to outline behaviors and conditions that increase the likelihood of developing a specific disease. A risk factor is defined as any variable that elevates an individual's probability of developing a disease. While risk factors often contribute to the development of a disease, they do not directly cause it. It is important to distinguish between risk factors and causative agents. Risk factors are correlational in nature and do not necessarily imply causation, as correlation does not equate to causation. For instance, being young does not directly cause measles, but younger individuals are more likely to contract measles because they may not have acquired immunity from a prior epidemic. Similarly, childhood obesity is a risk factor for diabetes but is not the direct cause of the condition. In contrast, HIV is the causative agent of AIDS, and the bacterium Bartonella henselae is the direct cause of cat scratch disease. When creating microchapter pages that link to the main page, include the following at the top of the edit box: `{{CMG}}`, your name template, and the microchapter navigation template you initially created. These links should be as specific as possible. For example, if a sentence includes the term anterior spinal artery syndrome, the link should direct to the page for anterior spinal artery syndrome rather than generic terms like anterior, artery, or syndrome. For further guidance on creating links, refer to the instructions provided [here]. Follow the formatting and capitalization guidelines outlined in the template. Additionally, the name of the disease should be included in the first sentence of every subsection. Overview Section The overview section must include the name of the disease in the first sentence. The purpose of this section is to provide a concise summary of the risk factors page in a few sentences. This section can mirror the risk factors segment found on the overview page. For an example, refer to the provided link [here]. Template Guidelines First Sentence: Begin with a clear and specific statement. Examples: If one particular risk factor is strongly associated with the development of the disease: The most significant risk factor in the development of [disease name] is [specific risk factor]. Other contributing risk factors include [list additional factors]. If all risk factors contribute equally to the development of the disease: On the overview page, use a complete sentence: Common risk factors in the development of [disease name] include [list factors]. On the Risk Factors microchapter, use bullet points: Common risk factors in the development of [disease name] include: [Factor 1] [Factor 2] [Factor 3] If no risk factors are known for the disease: There are no established risk factors for [disease name]. You may also wish to clarify the nature of the risk factors with a statement such as: Common risk factors in the development of [disease name] may include occupational, environmental, genetic, and viral factors. Common Risk Factors Section In this section, list the common risk factors associated with the disease. This section may benefit from the inclusion of a table. For instructions on how to insert tables, refer to the guidelines provided [here]. Less Common Risk Factors Section In this section, list the less common risk factors associated with the disease. Similar to the previous section, this may also be an appropriate place to include a table.
